Dates.text: Born in Cyrene, in present-day Libya.
Ptolemy III invites Eratosthenes to Alexandria to tutor his son.
Compares the Sun's angle at Alexandria with its position at Syene to estimate Earth's circumference.

Title: Eratosthenes measures the Earth
Body-Text: At noon on the summer solstice, the Sun cast no shadow at Syene but did in Alexandria. Eratosthenes measured the shadow's angle there—about 7.2°, or 1/50 of a circle—then used the 5,000-stadia distance between the cities, measured by surveyors, to estimate Earth's circumference at 250,000 stadia. The result was remarkably close, though the exact length of a stadion is uncertain.

Captions.eratosthenes-circumference.jpg: Diagram of Eratosthenes' method: comparing the Sun's 7.2° angle in Alexandria with its nearly overhead position at Syene.
